core_obligations: Retain the complete small general set-multilinear ABP construction for the author hard polynomial.
Apply the source Nisan rank-width statement to every possible fixed ordering.
Construct an arc pairing that splits a constant fraction of a prescribed balanced word.
Retain all four pairing-overlap construction cases and the final source rank comparison.
difficulty_reason: The authors combine the arc-full-rank ABP polynomial with a pairing-overlap argument that works for every fixed ordering, and use rank specialization and Nisan width bounds. The complete four-case combinatorial construction yields a nonroutine near-optimal n^(Omega(d)) separation.

dedup.scope: Full source identity snapshots have zero matches. Counted target is the near-optimal width separation against a single ordered ABP of any ordering, distinct from sum-of-ordered-ABP lower bounds. Supporting arc-polynomial construction is shared context, not separately counted.

compared.difference: Near-optimal width bound against every single ordered ABP versus lower bounds against sums of differently ordered ABPs.
